- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% of recent 7-day mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior 14-day high), model often overshoots; cap next 3-day forecast at 10% below peak or use 14-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment is positive but model shows flat or declining trend, model underestimates upward momentum; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment > -0.2 and recent 5-day avg > 70.
- Model frequently underestimates true price at 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile (±0.4 or higher); apply 1.5–3% upward bias if sentiment volatility > 0.35.
- When sentiment history shows repeated negative swings (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to account for delayed reaction.
- If model forecast is > 10% above recent 14-day high, reduce by 1–2% if sentiment is weak or negative; otherwise, allow for momentum if sentiment is strong.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds model by >5% over 3 consecutive days, apply 1% downward correction to next forecast to avoid overfitting to recent spikes.
